raw_response:
I've been farming these 5 mu for many years now. My husband helps when he's back from town work, but mostly it's me. Let me think about this year.

For wheat, I plant in October like always. I buy the improved seed from the agro-shop in town — the shopkeeper told me which one everyone around here uses, Jimai variety. I use about 15 kg seed per mu because our soil here isn't the richest and I want enough stand.

For base fertilizer before sowing wheat, I put down diammonium phosphate — about 2 bags for the 5 mu, that's roughly 20 kg per mu. It has both nitrogen and phosphorus. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I top-dress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, about 15 kg. So for the whole wheat season that's about 20 kg nitrogen per mu, 10 kg phosphorus, and I add a little potassium too, maybe 5 kg from compound fertilizer. My neighbor Old Wang uses similar amounts and gets good harvests.

Water — I irrigate wheat about 3 times. Once before winter to let it survive the cold, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. Our well water is fine but the electricity costs add up.

Pesticide for wheat — I spray twice. Once for aphids and once for the disease that makes the heads white. I mix them if I can to save on labor.

For maize in summer, right after wheat harvest I plant Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed — everyone plants hybrid now, the old seeds give too little. About 2-3 kg per mu. I apply compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu of the 15-15-15 type, and then urea again at big trumpet stage, maybe 20 kg per mu. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu.

Maize needs less water since summer has rain. I irrigate maybe 2 times if the rain is poor. I spray once for corn borer.

Tillage — for wheat I have someone come with the rotary tiller after maize. For maize I just plant directly into the wheat stubble, no tillage, saves money.

My wheat should give about 450 kg per mu, maize about 550 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For summer maize I plant hybrid seed into wheat stubble with no tillage to save money, use compound fertilizer at planting plus urea at big trumpet, and only irrigate if rain is poor.
